paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We measure the average similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models. We observe that the similarity score becomes lower as the size of S increases.

model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the relationship between a variable denoted as |S| and cosine similarity. The x-axis is labeled “|S|”, has a linear scale, ranges from 2 to 10, and has tick labels at each integer value. The y-axis is labeled “Cosine similarity”, has a linear scale, ranges from 0.1 to 0.35, and has tick labels at intervals of 0.1. A blue dashed line, labeled “Weight averaging”, begins at approximately (2, 0.32) and decreases to approximately (10, 0.23) with slight fluctuations, maintaining values between 0.23 and 0.32 throughout. A green dashed line, labeled “QLoRA”, starts at (2, 0.28) and declines steadily to approximately (10, 0.18), with data points at (4, 0.22) and (6, 0.20).
